title: Closed graph continuity for Banach linear maps
statement: Let $K$ be a field with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative absolute value satisfying the triangle inequality [def-weil-field]. Let $V,W$ be complete normed $K$-vector spaces, where the norms satisfy $\|cv\|=|c|\|v\|$. Let $g:V\to W$ be $K$-linear. If its graph $\{(v,g(v)):v\in V\}$ is closed in $V\times W$, then $g$ is continuous. Equivalently, it suffices that for every sequence $v_j\to v$ in $V$ with $g(v_j)\to w$ in $W$, one has $w=g(v)$. The zero spaces are allowed; no local compactness, spherical completeness, or finite-dimensionality is assumed.
